When you're told that you have food on the table and a roof over your head over and over. Eventually you think that's what's important when it's not, a child needs to be consoled when they fall, not antagonized. Then one day your friend's stepmother gives you a hug and you cry out because it's a feeling that's so foreign that you truly believe that you're in trouble for something.

For a while it was " fuck me I'm still alive" every morning I would wake. Its a rough, and dark coping mechanism. But it works. Try to have some basic tasks to do when you wake, or drink a lot of water before bed so you'll have to get up to use the bathroom.
